blogs.title: Distinguishing 'Right-to-Control' from 'Fraudulent Inducement' After Ciminelli
blogs.description: This post will analyze the Fifth Circuit's application of the Supreme Court's recent Ciminelli decision, specifically distinguishing the rejected 'right-to-control' theory from the valid 'fraudulent-inducement' theory. It will discuss how the court determined that inducing victims to purchase securities constitutes the deprivation of a traditional property interest (money), unlike the deprivation of mere economic information, offering a roadmap for prosecutors navigating post-Ciminelli pleading standards.

blogs.title: The Myth of the 'No Harm, No Foul' Defense: Kousisis and the Intent Requirement
blogs.description: This post will focus on the intent element of the fraud statute, examining the court's reliance on the Supreme Court's 2025 Kousisis holding to reject the defendants' 'no intent to harm' argument. It will explore the doctrinal implication that fraud is complete upon the induced deprivation of property, regardless of whether the defendant sought to cause net economic loss to the victim or whether the victim received something of value in return.

blogs.title: Securities Fraud in the Age of Social Media: Applying Old Statutes to New Schemes
blogs.description: This post will look beyond the doctrine to the factual context of the case, analyzing how traditional securities fraud laws are being applied to 'pump and dump' schemes orchestrated by social media influencers. It will discuss the court's treatment of social media followers as victims of traditional property fraud and what this signals for future enforcement actions in the digital marketplace.
